rv.q: But its flashing wit remains undiminished.
The play he created – rarely seen and never staged in England before now – is big in aim and meagre in expression.
Overall, this production of Rosencrantz and Guildenstern are Dead provides very little to criticise.

cn.t: Stoppard's existentialist masterpiece receives a mixed reception, with praise for its philosophical wit and theatrical magic, though some critics find the production doesn't fully capture the play's brilliance.
